2. The facts giving rise to this Rule are, in short, that opposite party Nos. 1-5 herein as a First Party filed an application under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in the court of Thana Nirbahi Officer, Maheshkhali against the Second Party-opposite party Nos. 6-14 herein for restraining them from entering into the land described in the schedule stating that the First Party men were in possession of 45.56 acres of land appertaining to M.R.R. Khatian No. 577 of Mouza Kalaramrchar on the basis of Settlement from the original landlord Ajit Kumar Roy; their further case was that the lands in proceeding were sea bed and they possessed the same by producing salt but the Second Party men without having any title and possession therein were giving out that they would forcibly evict the First party men therefrom and thereby were creating apprehension of serious breach of peace and loss of lives and properties. The said application was sent to Officer-in-Charge Maheshkhali P.S. who on enquiry submitted a report, Thereafter the Thana Nirbahi Officer by his order dated 14.3.83 drew up a proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure restraining the First Party and Second Party from entering into the land and attached the same and Thana Revenue Officer of Maheshkhali Upazila was appointed receiver. 

 3. That 2nd Party-opposite parties No. 6-14 filed written statement in the case. Their case was that the proceeding lands were purchased in auction sale by the superior landlord who took the land in his khas possession and subsequently he gave settlement of 13.13 acres of land of R.S. Khatian 579 to Sultan Ahmed, 5.00 acres to Badiur Rahman, 4.00 acres to Atar Ali and 23.43 acres to Fazar Ali from RS. Khatian No. 578, 580,581 and 582. The Second Party No. 1 and 2 claimed peaceful possession of 13.43 acres of land out of M.RR. Khatian No.577 and Second Party No. 3 was in possession of 4.00 acres from the same Khatian while other co-sharers were in possession of the remaining land. 

 4. The Opposite-party No. 15 was made third party in the said proceeding and his case was that he took: settlement of 30.11 acres of land from RS. Khatian No. 578 which was subsequently recorded in M.R.R. Khatian No. 577 and he was in possession of 29.31 acres after sale and gift of same land along with other recorded owners of M.R.R. Khatian No. 577 in which neither the First party men nor the Second party men had any title and possession and there was no apprehension of breach of peace. 

 5. The case of Added Third Party was that Third Party Badiur Rahman and Sultan Ahmed, brother of Tomiz Gulal took settlement of proceeding lands from the landlord on behalf of all recorded owners of M.R.R. Khatian No. 577 in 1361 B.S. and that they were in possession of the land in proceeding and there was no apprehension of breach of peace. 

 6. The case of the 4th party men was that they were in peaceful possession of their share of land appertaining to R.S. Khatian Nos. 957 and 582. Their further case was that the First and Second Party men being members of the same group managed to fabricate this false case obtaining a false 'report from the police. They further stated that there was no apprehension of breach of peace as the respective co-sharers of the lands of M.R.R. Khatian No. 577 were in peaceful possession. 

 7. The petitioners during the pendency of the proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure were made 4th Party in the proceeding. They filed a written statement stating that they were in possession of the land on the basis of their settlement from original recorded owner Khirode Chandra Roy and others and subsequently on the basis of M.R.R. Khatian. It was further case of the added 4th Party that there was no apprehension of breach of peace in respect of the proceeding lands and the proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not maintainable.
